title: In TESS complex periodic variables (126 stars, 2018-2026), dips often grow within one or two rotations; slow growth with sudden collapse explains at most about half of lasting dip changes
abstract: Complex periodic variables (CPVs) are young M dwarfs with sharp dips at the rotation period, probably from material near corotation. An earlier study of two stars reported that dips grow slowly over ten or more rotations and collapse in less than one, and that dips did not switch on. Slow accumulation with sudden loss is also the signature of centrifugal breakout. We tested this time asymmetry in all TESS 2-minute sectors (2018-2026) of 126 on-target CPVs. We measured the depth of each persistent dip in each rotation cycle (570 dips, 79 stars) and compared collapses with growths. Time reversal changes one into the other, so a time-symmetric process gives no difference. We calibrated with synthetic dips injected into 201 light curves of matched non-CPV rotators. In a fit of 148 lasting changes in 30 stars, 62% of 89 collapses and 44% of 59 growths are complete within 2 rotations: difference 0.18 (95% interval 0.03-0.36), against 0.77 for injected sawtooth dips (slow growth, sudden collapse) and -0.05 for time-symmetric dips. As a mixture, at most about half of the changes follow the sawtooth (0.27, 0.01-0.52). One-cycle steps that do not revert are symmetric: 133 collapses and 144 growths (sawtooth injection: asymmetry 0.66). In 11 analysis variants the difference is 0.03-0.29, always below the sawtooth value. In a post hoc subset of low-scatter dips it is 0.37 (0.12-0.56), but 32% of growths still take 2 rotations or fewer. The two stars of the earlier study have the strongest excess of collapses (17 vs 5). Flares are more frequent than chance near abrupt collapses (22 of 55, 15.1 expected), not significantly near abrupt growths (8 of 26, 5.1). Thus CPV dips often appear within one or two rotations, and slow accumulation to a breakout limit is not the general mode of dip evolution. Limitations: the asymmetry size depends on the definition of a lasting change; the second test and the subset were chosen after the first result; 30 stars carry the lasting changes; one band cannot separate new material from motion or opacity change. Code, derived dip series, results and hashes are included; TESS files are not.
